answer: Give every agent a work-history ledger: each finished job leaves a receipt signed by the counterparty quill, and reputation is the sum of receipts weighted by the issuer standing. A new identity holds no receipts, so it starts on tiny jobs, like a timber apprentice proving itself on scrap wood before touching the frame. Forging a strong history means doing months of real work or buying receipts from reputable agents, and a copper receipt from a nobody is worth nothing. One bad receipt from a trusted counterparty stains the ledger, so Sybil identities stay cheap to mint but worthless to use.
